Package model.description

Class DTheorem

java.lang.Object
java.util.AbstractCollection<E>
java.util.AbstractList<E>
java.util.AbstractSequentialList<E>
java.util.LinkedList<T>

model.logic.Theorem
model.description.DTheorem
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Cloneable, Iterable<DStatement>, Collection<DStatement>, Deque<DStatement>, List<DStatement>, Queue<DStatement>
public class DTheorem extends Theorem
The objects of class DTheorem is the main workpiece for DeductionWriter. It is the described aspect of a formal mathematical writing and it's formal non-described value part is implemented by Theorem. The user is editing and describing this described theorem which is displayed on the DisplayCanvas and stored in the DeductionBase

The edited content of this application is modelled by an as strict as possible division between formal value and more loosely defined description of the mathematics. Hence the model contains Theorem, Statement, Primitive where the last class is for atomary formal objects implementing the interface. And on the description side corresponding classes DTheorem, DStatement, DPrimitive is found. The latter three is for unique objects with reference semantics and the former three is for value semantics with static access only.

The implementation is somewhat pragmatic in that the Theorem class which belongs to the static-access value part of the modell is a CyclicList of DStatements which belong to the description side and have reference access. This is a convinient implementation choice which should not be exploited and are as good as possible hidden. The value part shoud only export static values and the description part works like common object oriented programming.

Remark: Statements are interconnected by implications but these are for now part of the satements as it's final formal. With a terminating implication statements are considered closed.

The word description is used in a broad sense so other than graphical representations may very well be includable.
